subject: HarborTrust - fallback policy + telemetry prioritization request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@harbortrust.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: HarborTrust - fallback policy + telemetry prioritization request

Samantha — thanks again for the demo yesterday. HarborTrust reiterated two critical asks that need to be on our roadmap for their dedicated deployment to proceed: 

1) Tenant-scoped fallback routing policy: when their reserved pool is saturated or we hit the latency SLO, they want an automatic, configurable fallback to a compatible (lower-cost) model variant *per tenant* with guardrails (max latency, max cost deltas).

2) Enhanced telemetry / trace attribution: every request must include a propagated trace-id and tenant tag surfaced in our observability pipelines and exported logs for audit retention (90 days initially). They also asked for a per-request routing decision log to reconcile billing and incident investigations.

They indicated that these items are gating (procurement sign-off hangs on them). Attached a short summary of HarborTrust's asks (harbortrust_deal_ask.pdf).

Can the product/engineering side give a short feasibility note and a target timeline? HarborTrust is asking for an answer by EOW next week (we have a CxO sync 6/21). Happy to set a quick internal call — let me know availability.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0118

From: Samantha Reed <samantha@harbortrust.com>

Subject: Re: HarborTrust - fallback policy + telemetry prioritization request

Vanessa — thanks for capturing this. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- For fallback behavior we need the option to prefer models within the same family (e.g., redwood-7b-quantized -> redwood-3b-quantized) and to set a SLO-driven trigger (p95 latency > X ms OR queued requests > Y). The primary goal is to avoid visible latency spikes to our customers during peak.
- Telemetry: we require immutable per-request routing logs that include: timestamp, trace-id, tenant-id, chosen model, and fallback reason. These logs will be ingested into our Splunk instance; they must be exportable via our standard S3 sink.

Procurement also asked us to get an estimate of engineering lift so they can finalize the purchase order. I've attached the internal security RFP for completeness.

Samantha Reed
Head of AI Ops, HarborTrust
samantha@harbortrust.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Eng Oncall <eng-oncall@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: HarborTrust asks — initial feasibility and rough sizing

Vanessa / Laura — quick internal note after an engineering sync: 

Summary of feasibility:
- Tenant-scoped fallback routing: doable within our routing service. We already support policy-based routing by customer tier; extending to tenant-specific fallback profiles requires: a) policy UI + API to store per-tenant rules, b) runtime check to evaluate SLO triggers and select compatible model variant, c) metrics/decision logging. Minimal viable impl (opt-in for Dedicated customers only) is estimated at ~2 engineering sprints (backend + routing logic) + 1 sprint for UI/perm plumbing.

- Telemetry / trace propagation: we have trace propagation hooks but don't currently persist trace-id + tenant-id atomically into the routing decision logs or expose them in the S3 export. Adding deterministic per-request routing logs + S3 export schema change is ~1 sprint (SRE + infra) for a scoped delivery.

Risk & tradeoffs:
- If we scope the fallback to a small set of model families and default fallback rules, we reduce risk and time to ship. Full configurable policies (arbitrary rule DSL) would be multiple sprints.
- Audit retention (90 days) has storage/cost implications; we should scope retention policy and possible compression/quarantine.

Proposed next steps:
1) Create INF-5421 with acceptance criteria (I added a brief outline; see implementation-outline.md attached).
2) Product sign-off on MLP scope (tenant telemetry + limited fallback variants).
3) Schedule a 30-min scoping with HarborTrust engineering to agree on S3 schema and canary plan.

Attachment: implementation-outline.md

Monica Patel
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eng Leads <eng-leads@redwood.ai>, ProductOps <productops@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: HarborTrust asks — prioritization and delivery proposal

Thanks for the summary — I reviewed the tradeoffs. Proposed product decision and target plan: 

Scope (MLP) — deliverable by 2027-07-02 if we green-light and allocate: 
A) Tenant-aware telemetry: persist trace-id + tenant-id into routing decision logs, create S3 export schema, and add a small UI toggle (opt-in per Dedicated customer). Acceptance criteria: exported CSV/NDJSON contains trace_id, tenant_id, model_id, fallback_reason, timestamp; test with HarborTrust dev cluster ingestion.
B) Configurable fallback policy (limited): allow per-tenant selection of ’fallback family’ and two triggers: p95 latency threshold AND queued-backlog threshold. Default sane values provided; HarborTrust can override. Acceptance criteria: policy applied in runtime and routing decision log records when a fallback occurred.

Resource ask: 1 backend engineer (2 sprints), 0.5 SRE for export + retention config (1 sprint), PM oversight (me). This is feasible if we deprioritize two non-blocking UI improvements currently in the sprint. 

Can product ops add INF-5421 to the roadmap committee agenda tomorrow? I will prepare acceptance criteria and a canary rollback plan (canary window 10% of traffic to HarborTrust tenant, automatic rollback on error rate > 2% or latency regression > 20% over baseline). Legal / finance need to confirm SLA exception language — I will loop them in once we have confirmation of funding.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear plan. Quick recap and next steps from sales side: 

- HarborTrust confirms budget to cover prioritized work in exchange for a documented canary and SLA carveout. Procurement asked me to request the SLA-exception-template.docx to start legal review; I've attached the PO cover note and the signed LOI (sending separately via DocuSign).
- HarborTrust accepts the proposed MLP scope (A + B) and can start with a 10% canary in production. They will validate the S3 export schema during the dev scoping call.

Action items:
1) Laura — please escalate INF-5421 to roadmap committee and confirm resource allocation by EOD tomorrow.
2) Monica — schedule a 30-min scoping session with HarborTrust DevOps (Samantha) this week; HarborTrust prefers Wed 6/16 or Thu 6/17 morning PT.
3) Legal/Finance — review SLA-exception-template.docx once I upload the DocuSign envelope.

If we get green-light from roadmap + legal, HarborTrust will sign the PO and expects work to start the week of 6/21.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite after Laura confirms.
